inspection_summary: Whole-source inspection of lines 1-714 found a sustained conformal-mapping program: analytic setup and fundamental-domain motivation; real-axis pre-image curves, strip structure, and color rules; construction of fundamental domains and intertwined zeta/zeta-derivative curves; a turning-point result; a claimed two-case Riemann-Hypothesis argument; and addendum observations from graphics. The plan records the paper's claims and mechanisms without treating them as independently verified. Formula OCR is mostly recoverable from prose, while several geometric arguments and addendum observations require later verification against the missing figures.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic metadata and an abstract announcing the branched-covering, real-axis-pre-image, zero-simplicity, and RH claims.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Sets up zeta, its pole, zeros, functional equation, the RH target, and the proposed fundamental-domain/global-mapping viewpoint.

sections_inspected.label: 2. The Pre-Image by zeta of the Real Axis
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops simultaneous continuation of real-axis pre-images, strip decomposition, color alternation, unit-disc pre-images, and conformal-grid visualization.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Fundamental Domains of the Riemann Zeta Function
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Constructs fundamental domains from expanding level curves and branch points, relates zeta and its derivative through intertwined curves, and proves the stated turning-point property.

sections_inspected.label: 4. The Proof of Riemann Hypothesis
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Presents the paper's symmetry reduction, induction scheme, and same-strip and adjacent-strip contradiction arguments.

sections_inspected.label: Addendum and figure-only tail
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reports graphical observations about fundamental-domain counts, exceptional configurations, apparent strip width, curve separation, and a proposed geometric quantification problem; several intervening pages contain only missing figures.

accepted_units.title: From the analytic zeta setup to a fundamental-domain formulation of RH
accepted_units.why_material: The passage assembles the series continuation, pole, real and nontrivial zeros, critical strip, Laurent expansion, and functional equation, then explicitly reframes the intended RH route in terms of conformal mappings of fundamental domains.
accepted_units.context_note: The formulas provide local setup for the source's strategy; the unit records the proposed change of viewpoint rather than validating the later proof claim.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the prose is clear, but displayed formulas contain normalization glyph noise and should be checked against the page scan before formula-level reuse.

accepted_units.title: Fundamental domains near an essential singularity
accepted_units.why_material: The source defines the working role of fundamental regions as domains mapped conformally onto a slit plane and derives the proposed accumulation pattern: finitely many meet a compact set, while infinitely many occur outside it toward infinity.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument invokes the source's earlier program and an enriched Picard-type statement; those cited works were not part of this isolated inspection.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: recoverable from prose with only the derivative notation and slit-plane language needed.

accepted_units.title: Simultaneous continuation of real-axis pre-images and the red-black curve encoding
accepted_units.why_material: This constructs pre-image arcs through zeros, continues them across derivative branch points, distinguishes the continuation stopped by the pole, and turns sign on the real image into a two-color encoding whose junctions mark zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction explicitly assumes the cited claim that zeta's zeros are simple; the paper also separates the interval mapping toward the pole from components continuing unboundedly.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: prose carries the mechanism, while some inverse-image and limit notation is OCR-degraded.

accepted_units.title: Quasi-lacunary value 1 and the infinite strip decomposition
accepted_units.why_material: The paper identifies 1 as a quasi-lacunary value, obtains unbounded boundary curves from continuation over (1,+infinity), and states that consecutive curves bound doubly infinite strips mapped onto a slit plane; the proof uses the unique pole to rule out boundary intersection.
accepted_units.context_note: Lines 180-185 give figure-based motivation, but the theorem and its pole-based nonintersection mechanism are stated in recoverable prose here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the curve labels and limits are readable, though the missing Fig. 1 prevents visual verification of the asserted configuration.

accepted_units.title: The j_k-strip inventory of zeros, one-points, and real-axis components
accepted_units.why_material: Within each strip the source distinguishes one component mapping bijectively to (-infinity,1) from finitely many components mapping to the whole real axis, thereby tying the count of curves to nontrivial zeros and points where zeta equals 1.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the combinatorial bookkeeping later used to index fundamental domains and adjacent zero configurations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low to moderate: the prose is complete, with only subscripts and inverse-image symbols affected by OCR.

accepted_units.title: Color alternation constrains remote branches, derivative zeros, and circle pre-images
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 2 imposes a common left-half-plane direction on both sign branches, and the source then applies color alternation to claim unique derivative zeros between consecutive trivial zeros and unbounded alternating components of circle pre-images.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit keeps the theorem's ray/circle justification with its two stated applications so the reused move is visible.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: the argument is prose-led; color names encode the signs of real image values defined earlier.

accepted_units.title: Unique unbounded component of the unit-disc pre-image in each strip
accepted_units.why_material: The theorem links uniqueness of the distinguished real-axis component in a strip to uniqueness of an unbounded component over the unit disc by taking pre-images of rays as their angle tends to zero.
accepted_units.context_note: This supplies a topological invariant of each strip that is later contrasted with bounded components in the addendum.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the limiting-ray construction is readable, but its geometry would benefit from the source figures.

accepted_units.title: Pulling back an orthogonal polar net as a conformal-coordinate visualization
accepted_units.why_material: The source replaces isolated real-axis curves with the pre-image of rays and concentric circles, using color, saturation, brightness, and conformal modulus to compare image quadrilaterals with their pre-images and to visualize repeating strip geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose identifies which quadrilaterals are unbounded and what remains invariant under zeta; the concluding methodological comparison motivates conformal rather than number-theoretic tools.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the semantic method is stated in prose, but its evidential examples depend on missing Fig. 2; later scan verification is required.

accepted_units.title: Expanding zero loops, fusion at branch points, and fundamental-domain boundaries
accepted_units.why_material: Starting from small disjoint pre-image circles around zeros, the passage increases the radius until loops fuse at derivative branch points, then combines pre-images of branch-value segments and (1,+infinity) to bound sub-strips that are declared fundamental domains.
accepted_units.context_note: The count of branch points and uniqueness/simple-zero statements are attributed to cited papers [3] and [9], not established within this span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the expansion-and-fusion construction is recoverable from prose despite noisy subscripts.

accepted_units.title: Intertwined zeta and zeta-derivative curves with color matching
accepted_units.why_material: The source overlays strip decompositions for zeta and its derivative, posits one-to-one correspondence between intersecting curve families, and combines color alternation with a cross-function color-matching rule to support claimed zero simplicity.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the principal bridge from zeta's mapping geometry to derivative directions used in the later contradiction arguments; its theorems are reported from [9].
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate to high: prose specifies the correspondence, but color matching and intersections are visually instantiated only in absent Fig. 3.

accepted_units.title: Symmetry reduces the claimed RH proof to two consecutive-zero configurations
accepted_units.why_material: The passage uses the functional-equation and conjugation symmetries to frame a same-height pair, divides consecutive pairs into within-strip and across-strip cases, and gives the induction by which those local cases are claimed to place every nontrivial zero on the critical line.
accepted_units.context_note: This unit records the source's proof architecture. It does not itself establish either local case or independently verify that the reduction exhausts the required configurations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low to moderate: prose is clear, though conjugation bars are damaged in normalized text.

accepted_units.title: Same-strip case: segment images and endpoint tangent directions
accepted_units.why_material: For two hypothetical same-height zeros in one strip, the source maps their connecting segment by zeta, differentiates its parametrization, identifies tangent arguments with values of zeta prime, and claims a contradiction between endpoint directions and color matching.
accepted_units.context_note: The parametric and derivative equations are retained with the geometric narrative; the asserted relative positions and half-plane directions depend materially on Fig. 4 and need later scan verification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: displayed equations survive with OCR noise, but the exclusion of the pictured configuration depends on an absent diagram.

accepted_units.title: Same-strip case: repeated crossings forced by horizontal tangencies
accepted_units.why_material: For the alternative pictured arrangement, tandem zeta and derivative images translate crossings into alternating horizontal tangent directions; the source argues that returning to the origin would force repeated crossings of the same intertwined curves, contradicting the segment geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a distinct obstruction from the endpoint-direction argument and is needed for the source's claimed exhaustion of same-strip configurations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the numbered points and crossing order are defined through absent Fig. 4-prime; later scan verification is required before geometric reuse.

accepted_units.title: Adjacent-strip case: incompatible tangent half-planes in two configurations
accepted_units.why_material: The source repeats the segment-image method for the last zero of one strip and first zero of the next, first comparing endpoint derivative half-planes and then using a forced turn toward the origin to claim contradictions for both pictured configurations.
accepted_units.context_note: The passage supplies the second local case required by the induction scheme and ends with the paper's claimed RH conclusion; this plan does not certify that conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the reasoning refers essentially to absent Figs. 5 and 5-prime, so scan verification of orientation and ordering is required.

accepted_units.title: Addendum observations on domain counts and unexpected high-strip geometry
accepted_units.why_material: The addendum reports increasing average numbers of fundamental domains in higher strips and highlights a bounded unit-disc pre-image component ahead of the unbounded one and curves embracing other curves as unexpected but allegedly theorem-compatible phenomena.
accepted_units.context_note: The prose preserves the qualitative observations and sampled counts, but they are graphical reports rather than a documented reproducible computation in this source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the claims rely on Figs. 6 and 7, which are absent from the normalized text; later scan verification is required.

accepted_units.title: Approximate strip width and decreasing average zero spacing
accepted_units.why_material: The source connects an approximately stable critical-strip width in the pictures with increasing zeros per strip to infer that average consecutive-zero spacing decreases with height while remaining nonzero.
accepted_units.context_note: This is explicitly an observed numerical-geometric heuristic, not a derivation supplied by the text.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the estimate and inference depend on the omitted graphics and should not be reused as certified data without scan and computation checks.

accepted_units.title: Apparent overlap of intertwined curves as a resolution artifact
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes apparent plotted overlap from actual intersection, attributes the illusion to curve separation below dot resolution, and proposes quantifying that distance with geometric-function-theory inequalities.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a useful warning that visualization scale can fabricate topology and a concrete proposal for replacing appearance with a quantitative bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the phenomenon is keyed to absent Fig. 8, though the caveat and proposed measurement are recoverable from prose; later scan verification is required.

v1_context_repairs.reason: The immutable v1 span starts at the theorem statement on line 355, but lines 349-353 supply the observed turning-point phenomenon, define the turning point as a vertical-tangent point, identify the positive-real-axis color branch, and state the theorem's purpose. Retain lines 355-433 unchanged while adding 349-354 as surrounding motivation; displayed-product and derivative formulas also remain scan-sensitive.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From real-axis lifts to a countable fundamental-domain partition
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source's reusable construction proceeds from simultaneous continuation of signed real-axis pre-images to infinite strips, inventories special components in each strip, and cuts those strips at branch-value pre-images into fundamental domains with one stated zero each.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The synthesis is internal to the paper and inherits its cited simplicity, branch-point-count, and uniqueness claims; it does not independently establish them.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Intertwined derivative geometry as the paper's obstruction engine
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Color matching between zeta and derivative pre-images, the positive-branch turning-point claim, and tangent directions along images of zero-connecting segments are assembled to exclude the paper's pictured same-strip and adjacent-strip configurations.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This states the author's proposed mechanism, not a verified RH proof; it depends on cited color rules, OCR-sensitive formulas, and absent figures whose orientation and exhaustiveness require separate checking.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Visualization as both structural probe and source of artifacts
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Pulled-back polar grids and high-strip graphics suggest stable conformal organization, changing domain counts, exceptional nesting, and shrinking visible separations, while the final example warns that plot resolution can falsely suggest curve intersection.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: These are qualitative or sampled graphical observations; the normalized source lacks the figures and supplies neither reproducible generation details nor certified bounds.

within_source_saturation: Every usable mathematical passage from the analytic setup through the addendum is represented by a new unit, the carried v1 unit with an explicit context repair, or bounded supporting context. Further segmentation would predominantly duplicate the same strip/color/curve mechanisms, isolate routine transitions, or attempt to infer content from missing figures and OCR-damaged display material.
stop_reason: The source-specific semantic inventory is exhausted after 17 new units and the immutable lines 355-433 v1 unit: the introduction, all three mathematical sections, the claimed RH case analysis, and all prose-bearing addendum observations are accounted for. Residual lines are metadata, headings, pagination, references, repeated visual commentary, blank space, or figure-only pages whose diagrams are absent, so stopping is based on whole-source coverage rather than a quota.
